Squaring the general form \(\sqrt{n+\frac{n}{k}}=n\sqrt{\frac{n}{k}}\):
\[
n+\frac{n}{k}=n^2\cdot \frac{n}{k}=\frac{n^3}{k}.
\]
Multiplying by \(k\):
\[
nk+n=n^3 \implies k+1=n^2 \implies k=n^2-1.
\]
For the 7th equation, \(n=8\), so \(a=8\), \(t=8^2-1=63\). Thus
\[
a+t=8+63=71.
\]
\[
\boxed{71}
\]
